clue.text: Old group walk briefly around school

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the band and the shortened walk back to front

parts.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band of the 1980s and 90s

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to march is to walk in a military manner

explanation.surface: A veteran band takes a short stroll around a school building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old group' looks like a description of former pupils, but it is the band. 'briefly' trims the last letter; 'around' turns the whole string back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A crammer is a private establishment that drills pupils intensively for exams, so it is a type of school.

clue.text: Religious leader — his name perhaps has power in church

indicators.note: in places the name and power inside the church

parts.note: Ali is a typical name for such a leader
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A cleric with a name of influence holds power in his church.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the chief civil and religious ruler in Islam.

clue.text: Quarrel makes one sound scared almost

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped
sound here means heard as, pointing to how it is spoken

parts.note: afraid means scared

explanation.surface: An argument makes a person seem nearly frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns the word for scared into a soundalike; 'almost' drops its last letter, the D.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight or brawl, a noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Creamy stuff annoys me? Wrong — excellent for eating!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters eat, or swallow, the other piece
wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: A1 means excellent, the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a rich sauce, then admits it tastes great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges the letters of 'annoys me'; 'for eating' puts A1 inside, the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a thick, rich egg-and-oil dressing.

clue.text: Wheel giving someone in boat change of direction (at the end)

indicators.note: a change of direction swaps right for left in the closing letter

parts.note: a rower sits in a boat

explanation.surface: A boat's oarsman swings round at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left) at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small spiked revolving disc on a spur.

clue.text: Little man has got hold of wrong gismos

indicators.note: the short name grips the wrongdoing, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: Des is a short form of the name Desmond
a vice is a wrong, a moral failing

explanation.surface: A small chap has seized some faulty gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gismos are gadgets or contraptions, which is what devices are.

clue.text: Fuss first to last over sprinter, possibly Bolt

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above
the opening letter moves to the finish

parts.note: ado is fuss
a sprinter is a runner

explanation.surface: A sprinter like Usain Bolt fusses before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks Bolt as an example of a sprinter in the surface; really Bolt is the definition, meaning flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, as when doing a runner from a bill.

clue.text: Green line going up to halfway point

indicators.note: only as far as the halfway point, so the second half of the word goes

parts.note: a vertical line goes upward

explanation.surface: A green line rises halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: Vert is the heraldic term for the colour green.

clue.text: Way little crawler comes in for second dance

indicators.note: comes in for means replaces

parts.note: a course is a way or route
an ant is a small crawling insect

explanation.surface: An insect crawls in for a second dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A courante is an old court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Rebellious lad's ready to abandon a job with horses

indicators.note: rebellious suggests letters refusing their order
to abandon is to leave behind, so one letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A rebellious lad is ready to quit his post at the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from LADSREADY and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddlery is the trade of making saddles and harness, work tied to horses.

clue.text: Haughty pinko with love for the East

indicators.note: one thing put for another means it replaces it in the word

parts.note: a pinko is a left-winger, a lefty
E is the abbreviation for east
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An arrogant leftie swaps romance for the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty can mean proud and condescending, a synonym of haughty.

clue.text: Wife facing criticism about garment

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke or criticism, as in a rap on the knuckles
round means about, as in 'round the house'

explanation.surface: A wife faces complaints about something she wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapround is a piece of clothing such as a skirt that wraps around the body.

clue.text: Fill our pan, mixing kitchen ingredient

indicators.note: mixing tells us to stir the letters of the preceding words together

explanation.surface: An instruction to fill a pan with something to stir in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain flour, without raising agent, is a basic baking item kept in a kitchen.

clue.text: Famous preacher to become wearisome for those listening

indicators.note: those listening hear the word, so we go by its sound

parts.note: to pall is to grow tiresome or lose appeal

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon starts to drag for the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle of the New Testament epistles was a celebrated missionary preacher.

clue.text: This person's beautiful female, friend in a majestic sort of way

definitions.text: in a majestic sort of way

parts.note: I'm, this person is
a peri is a beautiful fairy in Persian myth
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone describes a lovely woman friend and herself as regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperially means in the manner of an emperor, grandly.

clue.text: Spooner's regarding saint as a money-collector in town

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: marking means noticing or regarding
Peter is a saint, the apostle

explanation.surface: A preacher looks on a saint as a tax gatherer in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A street device that takes coins for parking is a town collector of cash.

clue.text: Words used to describe God in Warwick

definitions.meaning: God is described as both King and Maker
the Earl of Warwick, who made and deposed kings in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.definitionFit: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, earned the title for unseating and enthroning monarchs.

clue.text: Fantastic medicine, not new, beginning to prevent disease

indicators.note: fantastic suggests a wild rearrangement
not tells us to leave out what follows
beginning gives the initial letter

explanation.surface: A wonder drug, newly-launched, starts to stop a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop N from MEDICINE, add P from 'prevent', and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of an infectious illness.

clue.text: 12 came out making confession of sin

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disrupted

parts.note: 12 is the answer to 12 across, a famous preacher

explanation.surface: A preacher came out and admitted his wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'my fault', an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Congenial conversation in small rooms with meadows in view

indicators.note: the meadows are seen inside the rooms, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: pantries are small storerooms for food
leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: Friendly chat in little rooms looking out on fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantries are polite, agreeable remarks exchanged in social chat.

clue.text: Plant zoo animal in den?

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the den

parts.note: a pit can be an animal's den
a gnu is a wildebeest, a zoo animal

explanation.surface: A zoo creature sits in its lair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pignut is a wild umbellifer with an edible tuber, also called earthnut.

clue.text: Yarn in old magazine

definitions.meaning: The ... Magazine published Sherlock Holmes stories

explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a thread, and The Strand was a famous monthly magazine.

clue.text: Plant crop

explanation.definitionFit: The weed with broad leaves shares its name with a verb meaning to cut short.

clue.text: Various cities entertaining politician and Irish philosopher

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the shuffled word holds the others
various suggests the letters take a different form

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Several cities host a politician and an Irish thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges the letters of 'cities'; 'entertaining' puts the politician and the Irish abbreviation inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An empiricist is a thinker who holds that knowledge comes from experience.

clue.text: Friend's heart classically extended, in other words

indicators.note: the abbreviation is expanded into its full Latin form
heart means the middle letters

explanation.surface: A friend's heart grows larger, as one would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives IE from 'friend'; 'classically extended' expands i.e. to the Latin it abbreviates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'that is', used to rephrase what was just said.

clue.text: River coming from spring

definitions.meaning: to spring is to dash or leap suddenly

explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a Devon river, and to dart is to spring forward.

clue.text: Within a distance you and I must cross a nation to find foreign city

indicators.note: within means inside, so the rest goes into the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: to cross is to span, so the pair straddle the other letters

parts.note: we means you and I
UK is the United Kingdom, a nation

explanation.surface: Two travellers go a mile across a country to reach a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Milwaukee is a city in Wisconsin, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Notice nothing about Ms Rondstadt?

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the two pieces round

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells the singer's surname, which is Ronstadt.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda Ronstadt is an American singer, so her first name fits.

clue.text: Noisy talk from councillor over coffee

indicators.note: over means covering, so the councillor's letters go around the drink

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.definitionFit: Clatter can mean noisy chatter or rattling talk.

clue.text: Go steady, not half, on first of dates — having done this?

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: not means without, so the named half of the word is left out

parts.note: taken as written, the word itself
half here is the back three of the six letters of the word

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A couple go steady after their first dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the front half of 'steady'; 'first of' takes the opening letter of 'dates'. The definition refers back to the whole clue: courting couples have met by appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: To tryst is to meet a lover by appointment, which courting couples have done.
